First, we note that $x=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by $x,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+7}{x}-\frac{1-x}{x} & =4 \\ x\cdot (\frac{x+7}{x}-\frac{1-x}{x}) & =x\cdot 4 \\ x\cdot \frac{x+7}{x}-x\cdot \frac{1-x}{x} & =x\cdot 4 \\ \cancel{x}\cdot \frac{x+7}{\cancel{x}}-\cancel{x}\cdot \frac{1-x}{\cancel{x}} & =4x \\ x+7-(1-x) & =4x\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $x,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+7-(1-x) & =4x \\ 2x+6 & =4x \\ 4x-2x & =6 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $x=0$ as a solution. But since $x=3\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $x=3.$
